structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized single-phase austenitic microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations; metallographic analysis showed no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations.

unmapped_findings: In Fig. 3a, the yield strength for the 0–4 wt.% Al region (including Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al) stays roughly between the 350 and 450 MPa gridlines; the exact printed YS value for the as-homogenized 2Al condition is not given in the text or figure.

In Fig. 4, the 2Al (pale cyan) data points form a cluster at roughly 460–600 MPa tensile strength with elongation to fracture spanning ~8% to ~55%; this includes the as-homogenized 2Al condition, but individual condition values are not printed.
The mechanical values plotted for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP matrix (Fig. 3) are averages of three measurements for every material state, reproduced from an earlier publication (Ref. 49).

For alloys with intermediate Al contents (2–6 wt.% Al), the mechanical data fall between the behavior of the Al-free alloy (weakening/embrittlement on aging) and the 8 wt.% Al alloy (strengthening on aging); the 2Al variant shows a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior than the 8 wt.% Al variant.

As a single-phase austenitic TWIP (SIMPLEX) steel (30 wt.% Mn, 2 wt.% Al), the primary strain-hardening mechanism is dislocation-based hardening followed at higher loads by mechanical twinning (the TWIP effect).

A temperature-sensitive constitutive model for low-stacking-fault-energy fcc steels with mechanical twinning is presented (blocks b0036–b0100), but no sample-specific computational result is reported for this Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al as-homogenized sample.
